originalTitle: Violent crypto attacks rise as criminals hunt bigger payouts
simplifiedContent: There has been a big increase in violent attacks on people who own cryptocurrency, with a 33% rise in the first half of 2026. This means that more people are being targeted and losing money, with total losses of $124 million. The attacks often involve a combination of online tricks, persuasion, and physical force to steal digital assets. France has been the country most affected by these attacks. This matters because it shows that owning cryptocurrency can come with significant risks, and owners need to be careful to protect themselves and their assets.

originalTitle: IDFC First Bank Q1 Results: Profit shoots up 132% YoY to record Rs 1,075 crore; NII jumps 21%
simplifiedContent: IDFC First Bank just announced its quarterly results, and its profit is the highest it's ever been at Rs 1,075 crore. This is a big increase of 132% from the same time last year, when the bank made a profit of Rs 463 crore. The bank's Net Interest Income (NII) also went up by 21%. This matters because it means the bank is doing very well financially, which can be good news for investors who own its shares. This increase in profit suggests that the bank is growing and performing strongly, which could make its shares more attractive to investors.

originalTitle: Govt of Singapore’s India portfolio: 7 stocks rally up to 135% in CY26
simplifiedContent: The Government of Singapore has investments in the Indian stock market, and its portfolio is worth about Rs 1,51,353 crore. However, the value of its portfolio decreased by 25% in June 2026. Despite this, some of the stocks it owns, like Aditya Infotech, have done very well, with one stock even rising by 137%. On the other hand, some other stocks, such as HDFC Bank and Syngene International, have not performed as well, which has pulled down the overall performance of the portfolio. This change in the portfolio's value matters because it shows how the government's investments in India are doing, with both successes and struggles.

originalTitle: Metals Fluctuate as Middle East Escalation Keeps Bulls in Check
simplifiedContent: Here's what's happening: the prices of metals like copper and aluminum are going up and down because of concerns about a potential war in the Middle East. This conflict could cause problems for the global economy, which is making investors cautious. As a result, people who think metal prices will go up (called "bulls") are being careful and not buying as much. This is keeping metal prices from rising too quickly. The situation is uncertain, and investors are waiting to see what happens next.

originalTitle: Big Tech Debt Flood Is Taking Over Risk In Market: Credit Weekly
simplifiedContent: Big tech companies are investing a lot in artificial intelligence (AI) and to do this, they need to borrow money. They are borrowing this money by selling bonds, which is happening at a very fast pace. This is having a significant impact on the US corporate bond market, which is where companies raise money by borrowing from investors. This matters because it's changing the way the bond market works and who is taking on risk. As a result, big tech companies are playing a bigger role in the bond market than they used to.

originalTitle: IDFC First Bank Q1 Results 2026: Net profit surges 132% to  ₹1,075 crore; NII rises 21%
simplifiedContent: IDFC First Bank just released its results for the first quarter of 2026, and they're very good. The bank made a profit of ₹1,075 crore, which is 132% more than it made during the same time last year. This is because the bank earned more from interest on loans and had to set aside less money for potential losses. The bank's customer business also grew, with more loans and deposits than last year, which is a positive sign for the bank's future. This news matters because it shows that IDFC First Bank is doing well and growing its business, which could be good for investors.
